S05.meta: // SLIDE 05 — WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS TO VESSELS: Expected starvation vs observed normalization

tracks.label: Expected: uniform collapse
tracks.outcome: All tumor vessels destroyed; tumor starved of oxygen and nutrients
notes: Starve-the-tumor model predicts uniform vascular collapse
Hypoxia kills cancer cells throughout the mass
Does not match clinical or pre-clinical observation

tracks.label: Observed: normalization
tracks.outcome: Aberrant vessels pruned; residual network more normal, better-perfused
notes: Remaining vessels adopt more normal morphology
Window is time-limited — Jain's normalization window

S08.meta: // SLIDE 08 — FIVE ESCAPE ROUTES: How tumors progressively evade anti-angiogenic therapy

data.endClaim: Fewer than half of initial responders maintain durable response — five distinct resistance mechanisms each independently sufficient

S09.meta: // SLIDE 09 — IMMUNOTHERAPY SYNERGY: Does combining anti-angiogenic + checkpoint blockade improve outcomes?

data.question: Does combining anti-angiogenic therapy with checkpoint blockade improve outcomes?

branches.label: Independent pathways, additive benefit unlikely
branches.detail: Anti-VEGF targets vasculature; PD-L1 blockade targets T-cell exhaustion — parallel, non-interacting mechanisms
branches.fix: Additive toxicity without mechanistic synergy; combination offers marginal benefit at best

branches.label: Normalization enables immune infiltration
branches.detail: Anti-VEGF normalization window reduces immunosuppressive hypoxia, lowers interstitial pressure, increases T-cell trafficking into tumor
branches.fix: More tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes reach the core; checkpoint blockade then more effective on a primed immune population

resolver.label: Atezolizumab + bevacizumab: first-line approval in hepatocellular carcinoma
resolver.detail: The combination achieved superior overall survival vs sorafenib in HCC — the normalization hypothesis provided the mechanistic rationale for this first validated anti-angiogenic + immunotherapy approval
